items.text: Its new leader campaigned for the leadership on keeping the existing public insurance for doctor and hospital care and extending it to prescription drugs and to dental, vision, hearing, and mental health care.

Its new leader campaigned for the leadership on widening unemployment benefits within the existing income support, in which mandatory pension schemes replace about 45 percent of an average worker's net earnings, unemployment benefits replace about 48 percent of an average earner's net income in the second month out of work, and a single adult with no other income is guaranteed about 18 percent of the median income, housing support included: raising those benefits to 75 percent of previous earnings, paying them for up to 104 weeks, and letting more workers qualify.

items.text: Its leaders twice publicly demanded that the government sign public drug coverage agreements with all remaining regional governments, release the funding promised for them, and finish the first phase of that program.
Its new leader called for funding to extend public drug coverage nationwide after the government's spring economic update added none.

items.text: Its legislators introduced two bills to bring mental health and addiction services under the universal public insurance that covers doctor and hospital care.
